author: /root/path_scout_r51
body:
Caller/normalization findings (read-only; no code/tests changed). _source_tree_identity obtains _source_material_paths once during resolve_toolchain_context, then resolve immediately calls verify_toolchain_identities and recomputes it; every later verify recomputes it again. The same source-tree identity therefore depends on enumeration plus safe path checks, content/symlink bytes, mutation detection and digest framing; optimization must not cache paths or remove repeated identity verification. Git enumeration is selected from the supplied PATH, verifies the selected git executable before and after execution, and is bounded to 10s, 16 MiB output and 256 MiB RSS; it returns cached+untracked nonignored paths. Fallback walks sorted filesystem entries with excluded dirs pruned and depth/file caps. Downstream selected paths retain the 100k selected-file cap, per-file/aggregate bytes, symlink ancestor/target checks and post-read retarget check.

Legacy filter contract: consume the Iterable once; skip only empty raw strings; validate every other raw entry before any classification, including entries eventually excluded. Validation is Path(relative).as_posix(), reject absolute, any normalized '..' component, >64 normalized parts, or >4096 UTF-8 bytes; then deduplicate by normalized spelling, select by exact basename config names or .lean suffix excluding exact stems helper/Probe/Scratch or first component src/tests/scripts, then lexically sort. Path's public behavior is interpreter/platform-specific. Installed CPython 3.11 and 3.12 stdlib both collapse repeated separators and '.' components during Path construction while retaining '..'; as_posix emits slash separators. On POSIX backslash is an ordinary character; Windows treats its alt separator as a separator. The 3.11 source builds paths via _parse_args/_flavour.parse_parts; 3.12 uses _parse_path and filters empty/dot components. Avoid private pathlib internals. Edge: a sole '.' passes _validate then classification raises IndexError because parts is empty; with ('.', '../bad.txt'), legacy first completes validation and raises LeanToolchainError for traversal before classification. Any eager classification/filtering can alter this precedence.

Selection predicates overlap: config basenames anywhere qualify; any src/tests/scripts first component selects arbitrary suffixes; a .lean suffix can select even under .lake or a nested external-looking dir, except the three exact stems. The filesystem fallback separately prunes its fixed excluded directory names and prunes symlinked dirs. Symlink/content identity tests and environment/toolchain gates remain independently required. No new runtime dependency: pyproject has dependencies=[]; Python >=3.11,<3.13, CI matrix 3.11/3.12, backend uv_build>=0.10.2,<0.11.0.

The 20% gate is credible as a filter-only internal threshold on the captured real population: root's capture has 108,553 raw paths and 10,981 selected paths, making repeated Path construction measurable, and the alternating same-process median harness isolates that cost. It is still a deliberately demanding target and must be measured; it says nothing directly about end-to-end identity/discovery latency, where enumeration and reading/hashing selected contents also run. Keep the frozen baseline source, captured paths, interpreter and run order evidence together. Primary references: src/ladon/lean_toolchain.py:261-339,342-354,478-510,544-564; src/ladon/source_enumeration.py:79-124; pyproject.toml:5-27 and .github/workflows/ci.yml:16-38; local CPython 3.11/3.12 stdlib pathlib via inspect.getsource(PurePath._parse_args/_parse_path/as_posix).

Confirmed the #462 precedence trap with baseline code: _validate_source_relative_path('.') returns '.', then _is_source_material('.') raises IndexError because Path('.').parts is empty. But _filter_source_material(('.', '../bad.txt')) first validates both entries inside the set-comprehension and raises LeanToolchainError for '..' before classification begins. Eager classify-per-item changes observable precedence; suggestion is keep a regression for this pair (as scout noted in #464).

Additional fallback traversal probe: under a temporary non-repository root, with root file z.lean and nested a/Z.lean, _fallback_source_material_paths returns ('z.lean', 'a/Z.lean'), while sorted(...) is ('a/Z.lean', 'z.lean'). os.walk yields each directory's files before descending into sorted dirs; therefore globally sorting the fallback result as part of a filter rewrite changes the source-tree digest/order for non-Git fallback callers. Keep the legacy walk order unless a separately authorized contract change handles this. Also, fallback sees a non-source readme.txt at depth 64 and raises the normalized depth safety error, while it prunes directories at that depth so deeper descendants are unseen; exact excluded dir names and symlink directories are pruned wherever nested (probe src/skip/A.lean and src/tmp/B.lean => only src/skip/A.lean). All probes were read-only against the baseline module using temporary fixture directories beneath /home/codex/.cache/ladon-source-path-r51/falsifier; no repo edits.

Addressed the review in #479. I removed the duplicated validation predicate by centralizing the single check in `_validated_source_path`; `_validate_source_relative_path` delegates to it, while `_filter_source_material` reuses its normalized output. To avoid retaining one Path object per raw path, the filter stores normalized strings in a set and classifies those afterward, preserving validate-before-classify error precedence. This is the lower-complexity, near-baseline-memory option.

Updated scratch candidate: `/home/codex/.cache/ladon-source-path-r51/green/lean_toolchain.py`, SHA-256 `74384580d6c5d8d9fdeac784442a37a6dbc8a46ec44d913088d29cb3b261345d`; unified diff `/home/codex/.cache/ladon-source-path-r51/green/source-filter-optimization.patch`, SHA-256 `a01633c502cc47bbc4ecffd7b7f53611c4e97b3f6ac6652da32ee173906e5b98`.
